subQuestions.questionText: In an event of a severe fire in a restaurant kitchen, the first step will be to ...
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: A (1)
Route plan — In a severe fire the priority is life safety: evacuate immediately and help guests to safety.

options.A: evacuate immediately and help guests to safety.
options.B: quietly smother the fire with a wet cloth.
options.C: open all doors and switch off all equipment.
options.D: apologise to the guests and ask them to remain seated.

subQuestions.questionText: The initial baking temperature for choux pastry products:

subQuestions.questionText: The method used when making sparkling wine by fermenting the wine in a tank:

subQuestions.questionText: The method used to make a meringue by adding sugar syrup to egg whites:

subQuestions.questionText: During ... service, food is prepared on a trolley in front of the guest:

subQuestions.questionText: Read the statement: 'The majority of businesses use computerised stock sheets.' List THREE types of information that should be included on a computerised stock sheet.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any 3 (3):
• Name of goods/products/type of stock/brand name
• Description of goods/products/unique code
• The quantity/volume/mass that was received and issued
• The new balance (total) on the stock/stock on hand
• Minimum and maximum stock levels/reorder stock levels
• The price per unit/stock price
• A cash column/value
• Date
• Signature/authorisation/person requiring the stock
• Order/requisition number

subQuestions.questionText: Discuss the benefits for a chef to use a computerised control system to request stock.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any 2 (2):
• Less time consuming/saves time/quicker
• Easier to determine quantity of stock/more effective
• The system can alert the storekeeper of products that need to be reordered/manage and control the flow of stock
• The total cost of stock will be recorded instantly
• Stock will be automatically deducted from the stock list
• Number of errors is reduced/more accurate
• Stock control process can be carried out more often/frequently
• The computer can store the information/easy to retrieve information

subQuestions.questionText: Study the scenario: Luvuyo was appointed as headwaiter at the MARTT Hotel. After six months he received written warnings for being late for work and arguing with guests when they complained about his standard of service. Identify TWO ethical aspects that were neglected by Luvuyo at the MARTT Hotel. Motivate EACH aspect.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any 4 (4):
• Punctuality/integrity/reliability/productivity — Luvuyo was not a functional and cooperative team member/being late for work/not doing his full share of work/not being reliable and dependable
• Self-respect and respect for others/commitment/communication/co-operation/tolerance — He has failed to respect others/arguing with the guest/he was not aware of the guests' needs
OR
• Luvuyo was late for work — not a functional and cooperative team member/not doing his full share of work/not being reliable and dependable (no punctuality/integrity/reliability/productivity)
• Arguing with the guest — He has failed to respect others/he was not aware of the guests' needs (no self-respect and respect for others/lack of commitment/communication/co-operation/tolerance)

subQuestions.questionText: Suggest how Luvuyo should exercise good customer care.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any 4 (4):
• He must be punctual/give speedy feedback/respond timeously and efficiently/don't keep customers waiting
• Show patience/be tolerant with the guest
• Be polite/friendly
• Be positive when dealing with guests' complaints
• Stay calm/control emotions/be mindful of tone of voice and body language
• Find solutions to the problem
• Be reliable regarding guests' requests/not make empty promises
• Ensure guests receive value for money/receive what they ordered
• Recognise guests as soon as they arrive
• Display accuracy in taking and delivering guests' orders
• Listen and pay attention
• Be helpful/willing to assist
• Be alert to guest's needs
• Be respectful towards guests
• Make a good first impression/good appearance
• Accept his mistake and be apologetic
• Never argue with guests/the customer is king/always right

subQuestions.questionText: Read the case study: An outbreak of cholera occurred when people from a community obtained untreated water from boreholes, rivers and fountains. Even though education was provided in the community, a guesthouse owner continued serving food and providing untreated water to guests. Recommend how the guesthouse owner can prevent the spread of the infection.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any 4 (4):
• All water should be chemically treated/purified or boiled
• Provide bottled water
• Do not serve food and water that has been contaminated/avoid fish or shellfish obtained from contaminated water
• Foods need to be cleaned and cooked properly/use treated water to wash fruit and vegetables
• Avoid serving raw and undercooked food, e.g. uncooked fish or shellfish
• Cover food to prevent flies
• Thorough hand-washing facilities with antiseptic soap/sanitiser is important
• Staff should get vaccinated
• Send infected/sick workers home

subQuestions.questionText: Some people are more vulnerable to cholera and will become sick faster. Motivate the statement.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any 3 (3):
• People using unsafe water supplies/living in areas with poor sanitation/people who eat shellfish and vegetables from water known to harbour the bacteria will be infected faster due to the possible intake of cholera bacteria
• Children, the elderly and malnourished people are at risk because they have a weaker immune system/low levels of stomach acid that can't fight off the bacteria
• People living with someone who has the disease may be infected/higher risk of becoming infected

subQuestions.questionText: During the 2019 Rugby World Cup people hosted many braais in the spirit of the South African tradition. A local butchery sold the following meat cuts: LEG CHOP, CHUCK, GAMMON, RIB CUTLET. Identify TWO lamb cuts suitable for a braai.

subQuestions.label: 3.1.2(a)
subQuestions.questionText: Suggest the suitable process to soften the meat identified in QUESTION 3.1.1.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any 1 (1):
• Marinating
• Chemical tenderising

subQuestions.label: 3.1.2(b)
subQuestions.questionText: Briefly explain the process suggested in QUESTION 3.1.2(a).
subQuestions.memoText:

• Acid, oil, spices and herbs are used to tenderise the meat fibres

subQuestions.questionText: Describe THREE characteristics of good quality pork.

• Greyish light red/pinkish colour meat
• Flesh feels firm/does not leave a dent when pressed on
• Fine grain texture
• Fat normally white or creamy white/fat should not be oily

• The meat surface will be dehydrated/dried out
• Appearance of greyish-brown spots on the surface of the meat/change of colour
• Meat juices/sarcoplasm will ooze out of the meat after thawing
• There will be ice crystals on top of the meat

subQuestions.label: 3.4.1(a)
subQuestions.questionText: Motivate why the following rule is applied when preparing puff pastry: Measure ingredients correctly.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any 1 (1):
• To prevent changes in the ratio/proportions of ingredients
• Incorrect proportions can change the characteristics of the pastry — it becomes too hard/soft/crumbly/tough/dry/dough becomes sticky/to ensure a successful end product

subQuestions.label: 3.4.1(b)
subQuestions.questionText: Motivate why the following rule is applied when preparing puff pastry: Do not over-mix the dough.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any 2 (2):
• Over-handling/over-mixing of the dough will cause it to shrink
• Heat from hands can melt the shortening that can be absorbed by flour preventing proper rising/small volume
• Dough/crust will be tough OR hard pastry crust

subQuestions.label: 3.4.1(c)
subQuestions.questionText: Motivate why the following rule is applied when preparing puff pastry: Keep the ingredients and equipment ice cold.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any 2 (2):
• Cold shortening remains hard and forms layers between pastry layers/prevents shortening from melting
• Better rising
• Flakiness will be compromised if conditions are warm

subQuestions.questionText: Discuss THREE reasons for using the technique of baking blind when preparing short crust pastry shells for milk tartlets.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any 3 (3):
• Blind baking is done when a pre-cooked filling is used
• To keep the crust from blistering/rising/remains flat/keep shape
• To ensure the pastry case is cooked thoroughly
• To help the crust to become crispy/prevents soggy bottom

subQuestions.questionText: State THREE characteristics of successfully baked choux pastry products.

Correct answer (8):
Ratio of egg whites : sugar

• Pavlova: 1:2 / double the amount of sugar to egg whites (1)
Components used to assemble — BAKED ALASKA (3):

Components used to assemble — PAVLOVA (3):
• (a) Base: Meringue
• (b) Filling: Cream/Mascarpone/fruit curd
• (c) Topping: Fruit/any fruit

subQuestions.questionText: Describe the procedure to follow when melting chocolate.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any 2 (2):
• Chop or break the chocolate into smaller even pieces
• Melt over indirect steam by putting the chocolate in a bain-marie/double boiler/mixing bowl on top of a saucepan
• Stir occasionally
• Remove from the stove once water starts boiling to prevent overheating
OR
• Chop or break the chocolate into smaller even pieces
• Melt in the microwave by putting the chocolate in a bowl and heat in 30-second bursts stirring in between

subQuestions.questionText: Explain the preservation method identified in QUESTION 3.8.1.

subQuestions.questionText: State TWO advantages of using this preservation method.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any 2 (2):
• Prevents food from spoiling
• Increases the safe storage period of food
• Increases availability of food that are out of season
• Easy to store/no refrigeration is necessary
• Saves time and labour/no preparation necessary

• Transportation of food is easier
• Improves the appearance/gives it a nice shine/variety
• Improves the taste/unique taste

subQuestions.questionText: Complete the costing of a menu for 100 guests. Show ALL formulas and calculations. Cost of food: R15 000; Labour cost: R4 400; Overhead costs: R3 000. Calculate the total cost of the menu.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer (3):
• Total Cost = Food Cost + Labour Cost + Overhead Cost
• = R15 000 + R4 400 + R3 000
• = R22 400

subQuestions.questionText: Calculate the selling price if the profit is 50%.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer (4):
• Selling Price = Total Cost + Profit OR Total Cost + 50%
• = R22 400 + 50% / R22 400 x 50% or 50÷100
• = R22 400 + R11 200
• = R33 600

subQuestions.questionText: Give TWO examples of overhead costs.

Any 2 (2):
• Property rent
• Tax
• Water
• Electricity/gas
• Depreciation of equipment/maintenance of equipment
• Cleaning materials
• Stationery
• Post and telephone services/Wi-Fi
• Advertising
• Uniforms
• Linen: tablecloths, napkins or chair covers/laundry cost

subQuestions.questionText: Study the picture of a strawberry jelly dish (with strawberry slices) and answer the questions that follow. Name TWO factors that will influence the gel formation of the dish.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any 2 (2) — gel formation will be influenced by:
• Gelatine concentration/amount of liquid/gelatine
• Setting temperature 10–15 °C
• Whipping of the gelatine mixture
• Adding of ingredients: amount of sugar/acid/salt/number of strawberries
• Length of time before unmoulding/setting time

subQuestions.questionText: Describe how one can ensure that the strawberry slices are distributed evenly during setting.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any 2 (2):
• Allow gelatine mixture to thicken to a consistency of a thick egg white before adding the strawberries to ensure even distribution
• Ensure that the strawberries are free of liquid
• Small quantities of strawberries should be used
• Strawberries must be sliced evenly

subQuestions.questionText: Briefly explain the storage of the strawberry jelly after preparation.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any 3 (3):
• Cover the dish to prevent absorption of other flavours
• Keep the dish covered to prevent cross contamination
• Keep refrigerated until served to keep the gelatinous state/keep gel below 28 °C to prevent melting
• If kept for longer periods, the gel becomes firmer but loses water which will result in loss of texture and volume/rubbery and shrinks/must be served within 24 hours
• Do not store in the freezer

subQuestions.questionText: Study the DINNER menu (dated 20 June 2021, Price: R200 per person): Cream of Mushroom Soup; Steamed Hake with Garlic Sauce; Hungarian Goulash; Potato, Bacon and Garlic Bake; Corn Soufflé; Cauliflower Au Gratin; Chocolate Sponge Pudding; Coffee/Tea. Evaluate the choice of dishes on the menu by referring to THREE principles of menu planning.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any 3 x 2 (6). Food principles:
• Repetition of ingredients/starch, e.g. two dishes with garlic/corn soufflé and cauliflower au gratin both using white sauce
• Limited variety of flavours, e.g. garlic sauce and garlic bake
• Little variety of textures, e.g. mushroom soup, corn soufflé and Hungarian goulash all soft textures/no crunch
• No variety of temperatures — all dishes hot, e.g. cream of mushroom soup and chocolate sponge pudding both hot
• No variety of colours/no green or red — only cream and brown, e.g. cream of mushroom soup and cauliflower au gratin
• Limited variety of cooking methods — four baked products, e.g. corn soufflé, chocolate sponge pudding/potato, bacon and garlic bake and cauliflower au gratin all baked in oven
• Too many rich dishes/high in fat, e.g. cream of mushroom soup, cream/bacon in potato bake, cauliflower au gratin with butter on top
• Not all food groups included/no good nutritional balance: fruit group not included
Management:
• Time of the year/winter/June — dishes suitable as they are all hot/comfort food
• Availability of ingredients — all available during that time of year/June/winter
• Cost/budget is R200pp — price of the menu is realistic for the dishes
• Type of meal is dinner/4-course/time of day — dishes suitable for a dinner/4-course menu
Customers:
• Not suitable for people who follow a special dietary requirement, e.g. religious reasons, diseases, vegetarians
• Suitable for older people or children as the ingredients are of mushy soft texture/easy to chew
• Not suitable for small children as the dishes are too sophisticated or too strongly flavoured

subQuestions.questionText: Discuss the dietary guidelines that should be taken into consideration when planning and preparing a kosher menu.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any 4 (4):
• Kosher menus must not include meat from the hindquarter of the animal
• Milk and milk products and meat served in the same meal is not allowed/no consumption of milk products before 6 hours has lapsed after eating meat
• Shellfish, birds of prey and snails are prohibited
• Pork and pork products are forbidden
• All food must be kosher and prepared/slaughtered according to the religious law/meat must be washed and soaked
• Separate kitchen/storage areas/preparation areas/and separate utensils must be used
• Only kosher products/ingredients may be used
• Only kosher wine may be used in preparation
• Parev products can be combined with either meat or milk products or used as a neutral food in menu planning before or after meat/milk dishes

subQuestions.questionText: Read the extract: Joyce wants to start her own business selling sugar- and gluten-free homemade rusks to all her friends and family. After a few months, Joyce would like to expand the business and employ an accountant. List FOUR characteristics that Joyce will require to become an entrepreneur.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any 4 (4). Joyce must:
• Be willing to take risks/have courage
• Have an ability to identify business opportunities and take calculated risks to achieve success
• Be committed and determined/be hardworking/be able to handle pressure/be disciplined
• Have a sense of responsibility and love of achievement
• Be creative/unique
• Be self-reliant
• Be able to adapt/be a problem solver
• Be future-orientated/plan ahead/goal orientated
• Be confident in achieving success
• Have good organising and management skills/good leadership skills
• Have marketing skills
• Have high levels of energy/stamina
• Have a sense of humour
• Have communication skills
• Be passionate/optimistic about the type of business you are starting

subQuestions.questionText: Advise Joyce on the criteria to follow when using packaging as a marketing tool for the rusks.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any 2 (2):
• Information on packaging should be clear/easy to read
• Name of product must be clear/product easy to identify/brand/logo/contact details
• The packaging must attract the attention of the customer
• Interesting pictures
• Colours must be bright/interesting
• Writing must be clear, bold and eye catching
• Packaging can be collectors' items/reusable containers
• Information on nutrition must be indicated
• Packaging must be clean and hygienic
• Packaging must be suitable for the product/protect the product/easy to handle/strong enough
• Size of the packaging should not mislead the customer on the quantity
• Packaging must be environmentally friendly/recyclable/biodegradable

subQuestions.questionText: Name FOUR roles and responsibilities of an accountant.
subQuestions.memoText:

• Control banking procedures
• Oversee the auditing of funds
• Ensure payment of VAT
• Keep accounting records, keep track of money coming in and going out/do bookkeeping
• Safeguard the business's assets/financial stability
• Prepare financial reports
• Draw up budgets
• Prepare cash flow forecast/determine profit and loss
• Set up procedures for purchasing, receiving, storing and requisitioning
• Ensure stocktaking is done on a regular basis
• Take care of debtors
• Deal with financial queries
• Pay accounts

subQuestions.questionText: Evaluate the slogan below for Joyce's rusks as an effective marketing tool: "JOYCE'S best RUUSKS ..."

Joyce's slogan is a bad/no marketing tool:

subQuestions.questionText: Advise a restaurant manager on how to handle guest complaints.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any 5 (5):
• Complaints should always be handled positively and professionally
• The restaurant manager must control their emotions/be calm/don't raise your voice
• Be polite and friendly
• Maintain eye contact
• Positive body language
• Be helpful/show understanding and willingness to resolve the matter according to the establishment/take guest complaints into consideration
• Listen and pay attention
• Do not argue with the customer
• Acknowledge the complaint and thank the guest for bringing the matter to their attention/respect opinion of guest
• Attend immediately/act promptly/offer a solution
• Apologise sincerely
• Resolve the situation by inviting the person to discuss the issue in privacy
• Never place the blame on yourself or on somebody else
• Never promise something they cannot provide
• Keep the guest informed of the attention the problem is receiving/progress
• Report and record the handling of the problem according to the policy of the establishment
• Depending on the seriousness of the complaint or policy of the establishment a free drink/meal or discount can be offered

subQuestions.questionText: Discuss how staff members at a restaurant should deal with water cuts.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any 4 (4):
• Staff members should stay calm
• Apologise to the guests
• The kitchen may be closed during water cuts due to hygiene reasons
• Guests must be informed that food and beverages can only be served if there is clean cutlery, crockery and glasses
• Restaurants should adjust their menu to suit the situation
• Hand sanitisers should be readily available for the use of guests
• Bottled water must be made available in the restaurant
• Specific provisions/arrangements must be made for the use of toilets, e.g. collection of water from Jo-Jo/water tanks/boreholes
• Use available water sparingly
• Make sure that all taps are closed during the water cut to prevent flooding at a later stage
• Plan in advance according to expected water cut schedule, e.g. have disposable cutlery, crockery available/have containers with water available
• Follow the correct procedures to report the matter/report to the manager/municipality

subQuestions.questionText: Describe de-alcoholised wine.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any 2 (2):
• De-alcoholised wines are wines from which the alcohol has been removed/filtered out
• These wines are made in the same way as normal wines
• Before the wine is bottled, the alcohol is removed using a cold filtration process
• These wines contain less than 0,5% alcohol-by-volume

subQuestions.questionText: Read the scenario: During Covid-19, lockdown restrictions were placed on the sale and service of alcoholic beverages. Restaurants became innovative with the sale of mocktails and non-alcoholic beverages. Define a mocktail.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any 2 (2):
• A mocktail is made up of a variety/mixture of two or more non-alcoholic drinks
• It is a cocktail without alcohol

subQuestions.questionText: Explain how restaurants benefited from not being restricted by the general rules for on-consumption liquor licences when mocktails were sold.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any 3 (3):
• People of all ages/all religions could be served the mocktails
• Mocktails could be served or sold at any time of day
• Mocktails don't need to be served with a meal
• There are no closed days for the sale of mocktails
• The establishments made more money as sales increased
• No need for a liquor licence/no need to renew a licence, thus saving money
• Can sell it as a take-away

subQuestions.questionText: Discuss the closing mise-en-place in the serving area of the following: Clearing the bar.

subQuestions.questionText: Discuss the closing mise-en-place in the serving area of the following: Condiments.

subQuestions.questionText: Study the pictures (A and B) and answer the questions that follow. Identify the equipment in A and B.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer (2):
• A — Bain-marie
• B — Chafing dish

subQuestions.questionText: Compare equipment A and B. Tabulate the answer (EQUIPMENT A / EQUIPMENT B).
subQuestions.memoText:
Any 2 differences for each (4):
A (Bain-marie):
• Uses heat and water to keep food warm/warm up food
• Uses steam from boiling water, electricity/gas
• Has deep and shallow inserts/containers/bigger volume
• Flat lids on containers
• Used on a countertop or built in the serving area or in the kitchen counter
• Difficult to move because it is heavy
• More expensive to purchase
B (Chafing dish):
• Uses heat and water to keep food warm/warm up food
• Uses steam from boiling water created by wax candles or flammable gel/spirit burners
• Has shallow inserts/containers/smaller volume
• Dome-shaped lids
• Used on a buffet table in the serving area
• Can be moved/portable to different areas where needed because it is lighter
• Less expensive
